- When sentiment is positive (1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-day moving average to dampen momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (0.00) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to counteract downward bias.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply 1.5–2% upward bias for first 7 days.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days until sentiment stabilizes.
- If 3–5 consecutive days of high sentiment, model overreacts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day EWMA) to reduce volatility amplification.
